events.summary:
AQAFWD

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued
an Ozone Action Day for the Dallas-Fort Worth area for Friday,
September 18, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone air pollution in the Dallas-Fort Worth area
on Friday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by sharing a
ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive-through lanes, conserving energy, and keeping your
vehicle properly tuned.

For more information on ozone:

Ozone: The Facts (www.tceq.texas.gov/goto/ozonefacts)

Air North Texas: (www.airnorthtexas.org)

EPA Air Now
(www.airnow.gov/index.cfm?action.local_state&STATEID=45&TAB=0)

Take care of Texas (www.takecareoftexas.org)

North Central Texas Council of Governments Air Quality
(www.nctcog.org/trans/air/index.asp)

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by onshore flow restricting Kuskokwim River
drainage in combination with excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim near Bethel.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM AKDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
River or stream flows are elevated. Ponding of water in areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1252 PM AKDT, the river gauge at Bethel indicates water levels
above flood stage, at or above 8.5 ft. Additionally, reports out
of the Lower Kuskokwim, including Napakiak, Napaskiak,
Oscarville, Bethel and Kwethluk, confirm flooding in low-lying
areas. Water levels may drop with the outgoing tide this
(Wednesday) afternoon, but are expected to rise again Thursday
morning with another high tide cycle.

These high water levels are a result of the Kuskokwim River
back-up at its outlet in combination with heavy rain runoff
farther upstream. Minor flooding will continue from overflow of
poor drainage areas. High tides will decrease later in the week,
allowing the backwater of the Kuskokwim River to drain, lowering
water levels to below flood stage.
- Elevated water levels have been slow to recede. They are expected
to drop below flood level later this afternoon as the tide goes
out.
- For Kuskokwim River at Bethel:
At 11:51am the stage was 8.6 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Action and bankfull stage.
At 8.5 feet: Minor flood stage. Water starts to back up along Brown
Slough and flood low lying areas.


- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
